question: Can a target-independent 13-vector family selected for early coverage improve exact public-relation yield per charged group-add call on fresh prime-order fields?
candidate_vectors: All primitive integer (a,b) with 1<=a<=6, -6<=b<=6, b!=0, a+b!=0; sort lexicographically
selection: Greedy 13 rounds; each round pick the unchosen vector maximizing the sum of newly covered nonzero scalars by first-row offsets t=1..34 over the four calibration orders; ties break by lexicographic (a,b); preserve selected order as test order
baseline: The 13 nonzero-coefficient-sum vectors of the parent family in their original order
validation_selection: From prime p in [1501,10000] ascending, take the first eight with E:y^2=x^3-x-2 over F_p of prime cardinality q and nonidentity G=(2,2); all failures and checked p count retained
target_law: Exhaustive uniform nonzero scalar support d=1..q-1 for each validation field
query_law: First lexicographic row t1=0, t2=0..34, R1=Q, R2=Q-t2G; exclude identity or duplicate points; stop at first scalar-recovering relation
cost_boundary: For each target count tested vectors and abstract group-add calls from lazy t2 advancement plus each mul(a,R1), mul(b,R2), and combination through hit or cap; exclude target fixture construction and replay
falsifiers: selected vectors fail independent public group replay
optimized coverage advantage vanishes on fresh fields
coverage gain is outweighed by charged group-add work
selection exceeds the 13*34 finite-family coverage bound
claim_boundary: Group-only exact finite-field diagnostics for fixed target-independent vectors; no rational-lift search, CPU wall-time, or matched-rho comparison
